clue.text: In compartment stand opposite, looking humourless

indicators.note: the clue puts one piece in the compartment, so it sits inside the other

parts.note: a pod is a compartment, as on a spacecraft or for seeds
to face someone is to stand opposite them

explanation.surface: Someone sitting across from you in a train compartment wears a sour, unsmiling expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compartment' suggests a railway carriage, but here it is a seed pod or space capsule.
explanation.definitionFit: Po-faced is a British informal adjective for wearing a solemn, disapproving expression with no hint of a smile.

clue.text: Place at examination brings praise

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place in street names
an audit is a formal examination of accounts

explanation.surface: Getting a place after an examination earns someone praise.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of approval or applause, so the word is a synonym for acclaim.

clue.text: Makes available broadcast of icy conditions

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so the answer sounds like the phrase for icy conditions

parts.note: a freeze-up is a period of icy weather when everything freezes

explanation.surface: A weather report on the radio warns of a frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' could suggest an anagram, but here it means spoken on air: FREEZE UP said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To free up resources or time is to release them so they become available for use.

clue.text: Bed cold: that's painful

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
ouch is the exclamation when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone getting into a chilly bed cries out at the shock.
explanation.definitionFit: A couch can be a sofa or a bed for lying on, as in a doctor's examination couch.

clue.text: Birds' duet rudely interrupted

indicators.note: rudely means roughly and crudely, so these letters are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Two birds singing together have their duet rudely cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted' looks like part of the story about the birds, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is disturbed it has been broken into or interrupted, as sleep is disturbed by a noise.

clue.text: Pass round the port, my man?

indicators.note: the pass goes round the port, so its letters surround the other piece

parts.note: to pass something to someone is to hand it to them
a USB port is the socket on a computer

explanation.surface: At a dinner, someone asks whether the decanter of port wine should be circulated, addressing a companion as 'my man'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' suggests the wine passed round after dinner; here it is a computer's USB socket. The question mark flags that 'my man' is how a wife might refer to her spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A married woman may call her spouse 'my man', so the phrase is a playful example of the word for a married partner.

clue.text: Have you energy? Hurry!

parts.note: hast is the archaic form of have used with thou, as in 'hast thou'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you have the energy and urges you to get a move on.
explanation.definitionFit: Haste is speed or urgency of movement, so the noun is a synonym for hurry.

clue.text: Bear company and don't be swayed

parts.note: to stand something is to bear or tolerate it
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: Someone advises tolerating the people around you while keeping your own views.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand firm is an idiom for holding one's position and refusing to give way under pressure.

clue.text: A couple of lines on paper briefly make such a record

definitions.note: an adjectival description: the answer qualifies record, as in a record of that kind

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines give LL

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the last letter of the newspaper's name is cut off

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Writing just a couple of lines on paper could, briefly, set a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such a record' is the kind of record the answer names, as in an all-time high.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record is one never bettered at any point in history, the best ever achieved.

clue.text: Takes ages going to pot this red

indicators.note: going to pot means falling apart, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A snooker player deliberates for ages before trying to pot this red ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker players pot the red balls; here 'going to pot' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dithers hesitates indecisively and so takes a long time to act.

clue.text: A hairpin bend in seven reconstructed roads

indicators.note: the hairpin bend is placed in the rearranged letters, so it sits inside them
something reconstructed has been rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a hairpin bend is a U-shaped turn in a road, so it is the letter U

explanation.surface: A road engineer rebuilds seven routes, each including a sharp hairpin bend.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVEN rearranged ('reconstructed') gives VENES; 'in' puts the U-shaped bend inside to make VENUES, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad street, often tree-lined, so avenues are roads in a town.

clue.text: Quietly divide up onion

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet, so it stands for quietly
to allot is to divide up and share out

explanation.surface: A cook is told to cut up an onion without making a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small, mild member of the onion family, used widely in cooking.

clue.text: Party at son's place, a cheap lodging

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
S is the standard abbreviation for son, followed by the possessive 's
a place can mean a home, as in 'come round to my place', so a house

explanation.surface: Someone describes a party held at their son's flat, which turns out to be a run-down lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A doss-house is a very cheap hostel for homeless people, offering only a basic bed for the night.

clue.text: Take car and leave it here overnight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take the car out on the road
second meaning: a private road beside a house where a car is parked

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second definition as an example: a drive is somewhere you might park the car overnight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the verb for operating a motor vehicle and the noun for the short private road leading to a house.

clue.text: Sort of seat: dog needs it back

indicators.note: the dog needs it back, so the whole combination is read backwards

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dog owner explains that the pet needs its seat returned.
explanation.walkthrough: PUP followed by IT gives PUPIT, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-up seat folds up when not in use, as found in theatres and cinemas.

clue.text: Struggle of telecoms companies in 1939/40?

parts.note: a war between phone firms would be phone-y, and the dates are those of the quiet early months of the Second World War

explanation.walkthrough: The joke reads the name of the wartime lull as a fight among phone companies.
explanation.definitionFit: The Phoney War was the period from September 1939 to spring 1940 when Britain and France were at war with Germany but little fighting happened in the west.

clue.text: Flourishing growth of company that's hard to enter

indicators.note: the hard letter is made to enter the company, so it goes inside it

parts.note: a business is a company
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A firm is described as difficult for outsiders to break into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourishing' looks like an adjective, but with 'growth' it forms the noun definition, as of a thick beard.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushiness is the quality of thick, dense growth, as of hair, a beard or a shrub.

clue.text: Call to use metric in recycling centre

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a call to scrap the imperial yard in favour of the metre
second meaning: a yard where scrap metal is collected for reuse

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words the answer is a command to abolish a unit of length, which is what going metric would require.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrapyard is a place where old vehicles and metal are broken up and the materials salvaged.

clue.text: Others endlessly mull over; I have an answer

definitions.note: a description of the answer in the first person: someone who has a reply; a noun phrase standing for the noun

indicators.note: the others are taken without their final letter, cut off at the end

parts.note: the rest means the others
to ponder is to mull over

explanation.surface: While other people keep thinking it over, the speaker has already got the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of REST to leave RES.
explanation.definitionFit: A responder is one who replies, so the person speaking up with a reply is that kind of person.

clue.text: Don't be a burden

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hold back from doing something
second meaning: a burden is an old word for the chorus of a song

explanation.walkthrough: 'burden' suggests a heavy load, but its older sense is the repeated chorus of a song, which is also a refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for abstaining from an action and a noun for a recurring chorus line.

clue.text: Result of wound allowed to become a sort of fever

parts.note: a scar is the mark left after a wound heals
let means allowed or permitted

explanation.surface: An untreated wound becomes infected and brings on a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever is an infectious bacterial disease with a red rash, so the colour word names that kind of fever.

clue.text: President leaves a drop of red wine

indicators.note: the letter leaves the president's name, so it is removed

parts.note: Emmanuel Macron is the President of France

indicators.note: only a drop, the very first letter, is taken from the word

explanation.surface: A president departs after leaving behind a few drops of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a drop of red' is R, the first letter of red; 'leaves' takes it out of MACRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a French wine from the Mâconnais district of southern Burgundy, red or white.

clue.text: Daily, Charlie gets thinner

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
leaner means thinner

explanation.surface: Each day, someone named Charlie loses a little more weight.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'daily' is a cleaner who comes in every day; the word looks like an adverb here but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily, in British usage, is a domestic help who comes to clean a house regularly.

clue.text: Having no cover led Yank astray

indicators.note: led astray means led off the right path, so these letters are moved out of order

explanation.surface: An American visitor is led into danger without any protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Nakedly means in an unclothed or exposed way, without any covering or concealment.

clue.text: Fine fabric in reddish-yellow

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
lamé is a fabric woven with metallic threads

explanation.surface: A delicate cloth is woven in an orange shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Flame is a colour name for the bright orange-red of fire.

clue.text: Insignificant person, ruthlessly squeezed for money?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small, unimportant person
second meaning, a whimsical reading as 'pips squeak', from the saying about squeezing someone until the pips squeak

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'squeeze until the pips squeak', meaning extract every penny, was coined about German war reparations; read as two words the answer describes that result.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipsqueak is a contemptible, small or insignificant person, often used dismissively.

clue.text: On your bike — get moving!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to propel a bicycle
second meaning: ... as an instruction to start going, as a cyclist must

explanation.walkthrough: 'On your bike' is a British idiom for 'go away', which makes the surface an exasperated dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pedal is to push a bicycle's foot levers round, which is how a cyclist gets under way.

clue.text: Leaves with a double alternative

definitions.meaning: second meaning: in the phrase 'double or ...', the gambler's alternative to doubling

explanation.walkthrough: 'Double or quits' is a bet that either doubles the debt or cancels it.
explanation.definitionFit: Quits means on even terms, the outcome offered as the other choice in a 'double or quits' wager.

clue.text: Permitted not to pay anything yet?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: everything is still due

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer says the whole sum is still owed; the question mark flags the punning reading.
explanation.definitionFit: If something is allowed it is authorised, so the word is the past participle meaning given permission.

clue.text: Put straight crooked dealing

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who has been involved in shady business is set back on the right path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' looks like a description of dishonest dealing, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to bring them into a straight line, so aligned is the past tense meaning set in line.

clue.text: This selection produced all sorts of creatures

definitions.text: This selection produced all sorts of creatures

parts.words: This selection produced all sorts of creatures
parts.note: the clue describes the selection process Darwin proposed as the source of the variety of species

explanation.walkthrough: 'all sorts of' looks like a hint to rearrange letters, but there is none: the whole clue describes the evolutionary process.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural selection is Darwin's theory that species evolve as organisms best suited to their environment survive.

clue.text: Ruin of the French city sacked by Greeks

parts.note: des is French for 'of the' with a plural noun
Troy was sacked by the Greeks after the Trojan Horse trick

explanation.surface: An account of the ruins of a city the Greeks destroyed, told in French.
explanation.definitionFit: To destroy something is to ruin it completely, so the two verbs are synonyms.
